R10 leverages collider paths to determine orientations, ensuring that unobserved confounders do not bias conclusions. R6 and R7 extend this logic to handle more complex v-structures and path configurations. The interplay between these rules enables robust causal discovery even in high-dimensional settings where full observational data is unavailable. Failure modes arise when assumptions about path coverage or conditional independence are violated, leading to incorrect edge orientations and spurious causal inferences.
